### Team previews

#### [Harvard](https://www.shawlocal.com/friday-night-drive/schools/harvard/ "https://www.shawlocal.com/friday-night-drive/schools/harvard/") Hornets

**Coach:** Brad Swanson

**2025 record:** 0-9, 0-7

**Schedule:**Aug. 21 Reed-Custer, Aug. 28 Big Foot, Sept. 4 at Woodstock, Sept. 11 at Marengo, Sept. 18 Sandwich; Sept. 25 at Plano; Oct. 2 Richmond-Burton, Oct. 9 at Johnsburg, Oct. 16 Woodstock North

**Worth noting:**The Hornets carry a 16-game losing streak into 2026 after going 0-9 last year. Harvard lost its final seven games of the 2024 season after winning its first two games and ending a 20-game losing streak. Harvard was shut out four times and averaged only 6.3 points a game. OL/DL Braden Wittum, a three-time state qualifier in the shot put, returns as a starter on the offensive line for the fourth year. Senior TE/DB Brennan Peters will be “the QB on defense and ”understands the game plan and will be a great leader on the field," Swanson said. ... Other top returners are seniors Melvin Mercado (OL/DL) and Zach Bush (OL/LB). Sophomore Logan O’Brien will step in at QB after starting two games at the end of last season as a freshman. Swanson said junior OL/DL Jon Berkholtz is one to watch and will play center and defensive end. ... “The Hittin’ Hornets’ main goal is to play hard every play and execute,” Swanson said. “If we can keep guys fresh on the field and make plays, good things will happen. keenable.title: Girls track and field: Woodstock takes KRC championship, 1st conference title since 1998
keenable.snippet:
HARVARD – Woodstock coach Jon Brown had trouble stopping once he started mentioning names of standouts for the Blue Streaks at Tuesday’s Kishwaukee River Conference Girls Track and Field Meet.

The Blue Streaks doubled up in most individual events and cruised to the title at Harvard’s Dan Horne Field with 165 points. The host Hornets were second with 125.

The conference championship was the Woodstock girls’ first since 1998 when the Streaks won the Fox Valley Conference Meet.

Harvard’s Brenna Uplegger broke the long jump meet record with her 16-7 3/4 effort. The Hornets also won the 4x800 and 4x400 relays, Audrey Baird took the 300 low hurdles title and Abby Perkins won the pole vault.

**Kishwaukee River Conference Meet**
**Team scores:** 1. Woodstock 165, 2. Harvard 125, 3. Johnsburg 97, 4. Marengo 55, 5. Richmond-Burton 37, 6. Woodstock North 35.
**4x800 relay:** 1. Harvard (Rojas, Jimenez, McMillan, Koleno) 12:33.68, Woodstock 12:59.14.
**4x100 relay:** 1. Johnsburg (Casella, Alvarez, Meyer, Conant) 55.02, 2. Woodstock 55.31, 3. Harvard 59.25.

keenable.title: High school soccer: Harvard slips past Woodstock North in OT shootout
keenable.snippet:
HARVARD – Sliding a piece of paper between Harvard and Woodstock North might be difficult, the Kishwaukee River Conference’s top soccer teams appear to be that even.
They hooked up Monday in a game that provided a little bit of everything and ended with a thriling penalty-kick shootout, just as their two matches ended in the 2021 spring season.
Harvard’s fifth shooter, David Aquino drilled his shot into the net and the Hornets ran onto the field to celebrate a 3-2 victory over the Thunder at Harvard Middle School. It gave Harvard a 5-3 advanatage with one North shooter remaining, ending the match.

Harvard (6-4, 3-0 KRC) is quite familiar with shootouts, having gone to seven of them in its 12-match spring season. North is 5-6, 3-1.

Harvard took the lead when defender Brayan Mendoza blasted a shot from 55 yards that took a big hop over Thunder keeper Enrique Castaneda in the 48th minute. Five minutes laster, Gabino Esquivel sent a corner kick into the box that Silva headed inside the left post for a 2-0 lead.

**Harvard 3, Woodstock North 2 (OT)**

By Eddie Carifio
The Interstate 8 and the Kishwaukee River Conference announced a football-only partnership on Friday, combining the two conferences into groups to take effect in the 2021-22 school year.
Group A will be comprised of Harvard, Johnsburg, Marengo, Plano, Richmond-Burton, Rochelle and Sandwich. Sycamore, Kaneland, LaSalle-Peru, Morris, Ottawa, Woodstock and Woodstock North will make up Group B.

[ 4 ] [ 5 ] In June 2014, Richmond-Burton and Johnsburg both voted to officially become charter members of the KRC in 2016. [ 6 ] [ 7 ]
On July 19, 2017, the KRC voted 5–1 to remove Burlington Central from the conference, effective following the 2018–19 school year. [ 8 ] Burlington Central will join the Fox Valley Conference starting in the 2019–20 school year. [ 9 ]
In 2021, the KRC entered into a football partnership with the Interstate Eight Conference . The partnership creates two divisions for football, one consisting of the 7 smallest schools across the two conferences and one consisting of the 7 largest schools. In the 2021–22 season, the "Blue" division will include Harvard, Johnsburg, Marengo, and Richmond-Burton, while the "White" division will include Woodstock and Woodstock North. [ 10 ] The KRC will play its own conference schedule again in 2024. [ 11 ]
In 2022, Sandwich High School and Plano High School pledged to join the Kishwaukee River Conference, starting in the 2023–24 season, leaving the Interstate 8. [ 11 ]
